names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 decembrie, «Sfântul Ierarh Grichentie, Episcopul Etiopiei». The English form is chosen; doxologia prints only the Romanian spelling.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Δεκεμβρίου, «Όσιος Γρηγέντιος επίσκοπος Αιθιοπίας», with the rank word and the see left off. The page gives this name no gloss.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s second heading for 19. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Григорије (Григентије), епископ омиритски.“ — «Свети» is “saint” and not a rank, and «епископ омиритски» is the rank with the see, both of which BRIEF-SERBIAN §6 keeps out of a stored form. The book prints the second name in a parenthesis of its own and it is kept, because the parenthesis is the book’s and the fold reads it as one string either way (BRIEF-ADDENDUM §2). Measured before it was written: no other folder holds this key. The bare «Григорије» alone was NOT written: five folders already hold it — gregory-of-akragas, gregory-of-antioch, gregory-of-moesia, gregory-of-nyssa and gregory-the-wonderworker-of-neocaesarea — and the second name is what tells this man from them.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 decembrie — «Sfântul Ierarh Grichentie, Episcopul Etiopiei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Γρηγέντιος επίσκοπος Αιθιοπίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps, and the entry is the same man: of Milan, son of Agapius and Theodota, sent to Ethiopia at king Elesbaan's request and the converter of the rabbi. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. **saint.gr gives the folder its first years:** «έζησε τον 6ο αιώνα μ.Χ.», the page head «(; - 552)», and the death «πέθανε ειρηνικά στις 19 Δεκεμβρίου 552 μ.Χ.» — the same day as the feast. It adds his journey to the East as the great theological centre of the time, his becoming known at Constantinople to the emperor Justin and to the patriarch, his ordination to the presbyterate at Alexandria by the patriarch Proterius, the vacancy of the see of Ethiopia and Elesbaan's asking the patriarch of Alexandria for an educated and virtuous bishop, the rabbi Hervas whom he won and who was baptised in the king's presence, renamed Leo and honoured with the rank of patrician, and Elesbaan's successor his son Erdidos, who kept the same policy of reverence towards him. **It calls him «Όσιος… επίσκοπος Αιθιοπίας» and the see is Ethiopia as the page gives it; no coordinate is proposed for it, nor for Milan.** The rabbi, the two kings, the patriarch Proterius and the emperor Justin have no folders this reading could attach to and no `related` row is made. It prints no hymn.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.01.2026 (19. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Григорије (Григентије), епископ омиритски.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. Identified on four points this folder’s own life already carries from doxologia and saint.gr: a deacon of the church of Milan, brought by the providence of God to Alexandria, where the patriarch Протерије ordained him bishop of the Homerite land in southern Arabia on a heavenly revelation; the land freed from the tyrant Дунаан the Jew by the king «Елезвој (в. 24. октобар)», whose own folder carries a venerated serbian row for the Julian 24 October and the Serbian name form «Елезвој», so the book’s cross-reference lands on the corpus’s own holder; the baptism of a multitude of Jews; and thirty years’ rule of that church with a peaceful end in 552, WHICH AGREES EXACTLY with the 552 this folder already holds, so `dates` is untouched. ONE TENSION WORTH THE AUTHOR’S EYE AND NOT RESOLVED HERE: the Prologue heads him «епископ омиритски», bishop of the Homerites, where this folder’s `display_name` and `office` both say Ethiopia; the life inside the folder already describes the Homerite mission, so the two are the same see under two names, and NOTHING was changed — an `office` string costs four locale translations a reader may not invent. NO `related` ROW WAS ADDED to Елезвој although the book’s cross-reference and this folder’s own prose would both carry one: that folder holds no row to him either, the gap predates this reading, and it is reported rather than written. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026).

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Γρηγέντιος πέθανε ειρηνικά στις 19 Δεκεμβρίου 552 μ.Χ. και τη στέρησή του, θρήνησε πολύς κόσμος», with «(; - 552)» in the page head and «έζησε τον 6ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» in its first sentence. No year of birth is given. The folder held no dates before this reading.
